newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan electronic shares plunge, many limit-down.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan electronic shares plunge, many limit-down.

text.p: Shares in Taiwan's star electronics sector plunged in late trading on Thursday, defying what brokers called obvious government intervention to support the volatile market in the face of political uncertainties.
With 30 minutes of trading to go, at 0330 GMT, the sector was down 6.07 percent -- more than triple a 1.72 percent downturn in the overall market.
Many key electronics companies saw their shares tumble by the daily maximum limit of seven percent.
The island's top chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor was limit-down to T$100.5. The second-biggest, United Microelectronics, was also limit down at T$64.5.
The two were the most heavily traded shares on the morning.

The electronics downturn stood in sharp contrast to a 0.70 percent rise in the most heavily weighted financial sector, the target of aggressive buying by government-related funds in an what brokers called an obvious effort to support the index.

Brokers attributed the yawning downturn to a general recent softening in prices for key electronic products and components, chiefly CD-ROMs, notebook computers and motherboards -- all of which are made in huge numbers in Taiwan.
Profit-taking against the sector's recent gains was another factor, they said.

The electronics sector, featuring some of the island's most profitable firms, has generally been at the forefront of a sustained rally that has added more than 60 percent to the main index since March 1996.
